source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
source.citation: Toru Koizumi, Toshiki Maekawa, Masanari Mizuno, Maru Kuroki, Tomoaki Tsumura, and Ryota Shioya. 2025. RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables. In Proceedings of the 6th Championship Branch Prediction (CBP 2025), in conjunction with ISCA 2025, June 21, 2025, Tokyo, Japan, pp. 1-6.

summary: The 'sr' (sR) component is a statistical corrector (SC) extension that captures correlations between branch directions and recently produced register values without explicitly tracking data dependencies. It maintains a Tomasulo-like tracking table of 65 logical registers, recording either pending ROB indices or 12-bit value digests that decay after 256 decoded instructions. The component is partitioned into 8 banks of registers. For each bank, 3 usefulness tables (UT) evaluate which available register is most predictive; the digest of the most useful register is hashed with the branch PC to index 3 prediction weight tables (WT). The bank sum is scaled by 2.5 if judged useful (or 0 if not), and all bank outputs are summed into the SC partial sum sR, providing substantial accuracy gains particularly immediately after branch misprediction recovery.

state.name: wt_tables
state.organization: 8 banks, each containing 3 direct-mapped weight tables: WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), WT2 (128 entries). Total entries across all 8 banks = 8 * (512 + 256 + 128) = 7,168 entries
state.indexing: Hashed from branch PC and the selected 12-bit register digest: h0(PC, digest) produces 9-bit index for WT0 (512 entries); h1(PC, digest) produces 8-bit index for WT1 (256 entries); h2(PC, digest) produces 7-bit index for WT2 (128 entries)

state.name: ut_tables
state.organization: 8 banks, each containing 3 direct-mapped usefulness tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) of 8 entries each. Each entry contains a vector of usefulness weights corresponding to the logical registers assigned to that bank (Bank 0 tracks 9 registers R0, R8, ..., R64; Banks 1-7 track 8 registers each, totaling 65 registers)
state.entry_format: Vector of 6-bit signed saturating usefulness weights [-32, 31]: 9 x 6-bit weights per entry in Bank 0 (54 bits/entry); 8 x 6-bit weights per entry in Banks 1-7 (48 bits/entry). Total entries = 65 registers * 3 tables * 8 entries = 1,560 individual 6-bit weights
state.indexing: Branch PC folded/skewed with 3 distinct hash functions to produce 3-bit indices [2:0] for UT0, UT1, and UT2

state.name: register_tracking_table
state.organization: Direct-mapped table with 65 entries indexed by architectural/logical register ID (R0 to R64)
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit), payload (14 bits: holds 14-bit ROB index when valid=0, or 12-bit digest when valid=1), decay_ctr (8-bit down-counter initialized to 256)
state.indexing: Direct indexing by logical register ID (0 to 64)

algorithms.name: digest_generation
algorithms.trigger: Instruction execution / completion when a register result value is produced
algorithms.notes: Outputs a 12-bit digest. Integer registers XOR-fold trailing count, leading count, and 6 LSBs. FP registers extract sign and high exponent bits aligned at digest bit 3. Flag registers replicate 4 bits across all 12 bits.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.trigger: Lookup time (fetch/decode stage for branch prediction)
algorithms.notes: The sR partial sum is forwarded to the SC final adder, combining with sB, sG, sP, sC, sI, sL, sS, and sT to produce LSUM. Only registers marked valid and not decayed are candidates.

algorithms.name: instruction_decode
algorithms.trigger: Decode time for every instruction in execution stream
algorithms.notes: Maintains register availability using Tomasulo-like tag tracking. Each digest decays and is invalidated after 256 subsequent decoded instructions.

algorithms.name: instruction_complete
algorithms.trigger: Execution complete / writeback for producing instruction
algorithms.notes: Makes register digest available for subsequent branch predictions prior to commit.

algorithms.name: update_and_train
algorithms.trigger: Branch commit / SC update time (when SC training threshold requires update)
algorithms.pseudocode:
function update_sr(pc: uint64, actual_taken: bool, available_regs_at_pred: Array[Set[uint8]], selected_regs_at_pred: Array[uint8]):
    for bank_idx in 0..7:
        available = available_regs_at_pred[bank_idx]
        if available.is_empty():
            continue
            
        // Single write-port constraint: randomly pick one available register to update
        reg_to_update = random_select(available)
        digest = register_tracking_table[reg_to_update].payload[11:0]
        
        h0 = hash_wt0(pc, digest)
        h1 = hash_wt1(pc, digest)
        h2 = hash_wt2(pc, digest)
        
        // Update WT prediction weights
        step = actual_taken ? +1 : -1
        wt_tables[bank_idx].WT0[h0] = saturate_signed_6bit(wt_tables[bank_idx].WT0[h0] + step)
        wt_tables[bank_idx].WT1[h1] = saturate_signed_6bit(wt_tables[bank_idx].WT1[h1] + step)
        wt_tables[bank_idx].WT2[h2] = saturate_signed_6bit(wt_tables[bank_idx].WT2[h2] + step)
        
        // Update UT usefulness weights for the selected register
        ut0_idx = hash_ut0(pc)
        ut1_idx = hash_ut1(pc)
        ut2_idx = hash_ut2(pc)
        
        // Useful if WT direction matched actual branch outcome
        pred_agreed = (wt_tables[bank_idx].WT0[h0] + wt_tables[bank_idx].WT1[h1] + wt_tables[bank_idx].WT2[h2] >= 0) == actual_taken
        u_step = pred_agreed ? +1 : -1
        ut_tables[bank_idx].UT0[ut0_idx][reg_to_update] = saturate_signed_6bit(ut_tables[bank_idx].UT0[ut0_idx][reg_to_update] + u_step)
        ut_tables[bank_idx].UT1[ut1_idx][reg_to_update] = saturate_signed_6bit(ut_tables[bank_idx].UT1[ut1_idx][reg_to_update] + u_step)
        ut_tables[bank_idx].UT2[ut2_idx][reg_to_update] = saturate_signed_6bit(ut_tables[bank_idx].UT2[ut2_idx][reg_to_update] + u_step)
algorithms.notes: Correlations are trained only for registers that were valid and available at prediction time. If multiple registers in a bank were available, one is chosen at random to enforce a single write port per table.

algorithms.name: mispredict_recovery
algorithms.notes: Instructions that finished execution prior to the branch misprediction resolution preserve their valid digests in the tracking table, expanding the visible register state upon pipeline restart.

host_interfaces.description: Notification of each instruction decoded, including destination logical register ID and allocated ROB index.
host_interfaces.fallback: If decode notification is unavailable, capture at dispatch/rename; if ROB index is unavailable, track with an in-order sequence tag.

host_interfaces.description: Signal when an instruction completes execution in the functional units, providing the allocated ROB index, destination logical register ID, register data type (INT, FP, FLAG), and the 64-bit result value.
host_interfaces.fallback: Snoop the common data bus / writeback bus; if register type is not provided by host, treat all general-purpose registers as INT.

host_interfaces.description: Signal on misprediction flush specifying the range or set of squashed ROB indices.
host_interfaces.fallback: On any pipeline flush, invalidate all pending entries (valid == 0).

host_interfaces.description: Interface to the SC summation tree to inject the sR partial sum into LSUM, and branch update metadata containing available register IDs at prediction time.
host_interfaces.fallback: Standard SC interface; if available register metadata cannot be queued in branch prediction payload, re-read currently valid registers at update time.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: WT tables: 6 bits * (512 + 256 + 128 entries) * 8 banks = 43,008 bits. UT tables: 6 bits * 65 registers * (8 + 8 + 8 entries) = 9,360 bits. Register tracking table: 65 registers * (1 valid bit + 14-bit payload + 8-bit decay counter) = 1,495 bits. Total = 43,008 + 9,360 + 1,495 = 53,863 bits (6.57 KiB).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Requires 12-bit digest generation logic (leading/trailing zero counters, XOR gates, bit extraction), skewed PC hash generators for UT (3-bit) and WT (7, 8, 9-bit), max-selection logic across up to 9 registers per bank, a 2.5x fixed-point multiplier per bank ((x << 1) + (x >> 1)), and an 8-input adder tree to sum bank contributions into sR.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: In an iso-storage budget (e.g. 192 KiB), storage can be reclaimed by removing ~1.5 high tagged banks from TAGE (each 2K-entry high bank is 34,816 bits) or reducing base Bimodal table capacity.

parameters.name: num_banks
parameters.storage_impact: Scales WT capacity and UT bank organization proportionally

parameters.name: num_logical_registers
parameters.storage_impact: Directly scales UT entry width and register tracking table storage (23 bits per register)

parameters.name: decay_instructions
parameters.storage_impact: Sets decay_ctr width = ceil(log2(decay_instructions)) bits in register tracking table

parameters.name: useful_multiplier
parameters.storage_impact: No storage impact (combinational scaling multiplier logic)

unit_tests.name: test_int_digest_generation
unit_tests.given: An integer register producing 64-bit value 0x0000000000000008 (trailing zeros = 3, leading zeros = 60, LSB6 = 0x08).

unit_tests.name: test_flag_digest_generation
unit_tests.given: A condition-code register producing 4-bit flag pattern 0b1011.
unit_tests.expect: Computed 12-bit digest replicates the 4-bit field three times: 0b101110111011 (0xBBB).

unit_tests.name: test_bank_register_selection
unit_tests.given: Bank 0 has two valid registers R0 and R8. UT tables for branch PC produce summed usefulness of +5 for R0 and +12 for R8.
unit_tests.expect: Bank 0 selects R8 as the most useful register, and hashes (PC, digest(R8)) to query WT0, WT1, and WT2.

unit_tests.name: test_usefulness_scaling_zero
unit_tests.given: Bank 1 has one valid register R1 with summed usefulness of -2 (non-positive). WT tables produce sum +10.
unit_tests.expect: Because usefulness is non-positive, multiplier selects x0 and Bank 1 contributes 0 to sR.

unit_tests.name: test_usefulness_scaling_positive
unit_tests.given: Bank 1 has one valid register R1 with summed usefulness of +4. WT tables produce sum +10.
unit_tests.expect: Because usefulness is positive, multiplier scales by 2.5 and Bank 1 contributes int(10 * 2.5) = 25 to sR.

unit_tests.name: test_decay_invalidation
unit_tests.given: Register R5 receives a valid digest at instruction cycle T with decay_ctr initialized to 256. 256 subsequent instructions are decoded without any new write to R5.
unit_tests.expect: After 256 decodes, decay_ctr reaches 0 and valid bit is cleared; R5 is no longer considered available for prediction.

unit_tests.name: test_mispredict_visibility
unit_tests.given: Branch B1 mispredicts. An older in-flight instruction I0 targeting R2 completed execution and wrote its digest before B1 resolved, while speculative instruction I1 targeting R3 was squashed.
unit_tests.expect: Upon pipeline restart, R2 remains valid with its computed digest and participates in predicting branches following the restart, while R3 is invalidated.

open_questions: Count encoding for integer digests: The paper specifies a 6-bit field for trailing and leading zeros (or ones), but a 64-bit register has 0..64 identical bits (requiring 7 bits). Whether the count is saturated at 63, truncated modulo 64, or counts bits matching MSB/LSB is assumed to be saturation at 63.

FP format classification and unaligned formats: The mechanism for classifying FP16/FP32/FP64 using MSBs in general-purpose registers is not specified in detail, nor is the handling of denormals or non-float bit patterns.

Per-bank usefulness multiplier trigger condition: Figure 5(c) indicates 'x0 or x2.5' per bank. It is inferred that the condition is (max_usefulness > 0), but whether it relies on a non-zero threshold or a global enable is not explicitly formalized.
Hash functions for skewed PC and (PC + digest): The exact bit permutations and fold polynomials for UT0..UT2 and WT0..WT2 indices are not given in the paper and must be defined during integration.

Random selection policy: The paper specifies that during training, if multiple registers in a bank were available, one is selected randomly. The exact PRNG source (e.g. using the 64-bit seed from Table 2) is assumed.
